correctness.rationale: The failure-cap equivalence is proved bidirectionally. Its 136 caps enumerate all possible open-neighbor total domination and closed-signature separation failures. Cap intersections additionally prove the tail coefficients; no statement extrapolates to infinite graphs.

value.rationale: The joint code family is a natural established graph property and its exact polynomial on the canonical strongly regular (16,6,2,2) pair exposes differences unseen in their identical total-domination polynomials. Counts reverse in sizes 6,7,8 and agree from 9 upwards, with a proven local-cap explanation for the common tail. This is meaningful finite structural discrimination, not a copied scalar count or unmotivated slice.
